newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ABB says to build $30 mln Brazil plant.
newsitem.headline: ABB says to build $30 mln Brazil plant.

text.p: Swedish-Swiss electrical engineering firm ABB AG said it plans to invest $38 million in Brazil by 1998, including $30 million to build a new factory to produce electrical towers in Minas Gerais state.
In a statement, the firm said the new factory at Betim, which will begin operating in January 1998, will double its output of towers to 25,000 tonnes a year.
The company also plans to spend $8 million on its Guarulhos plant in Sao Paulo state -- $5 million for modernization and $3 million on environmental control, according to the statement.

The new Betim plant, which will substitute ABB's Contagem plant, which was inaugurated in 1970, "is the most modern in the group," Fernando Terni, superintendent of transmission and distribution for ABB in Brazil was quoted as saying.
To boost tower output the firm also has leased a factory from Mendes Junior construction firm in Belo Horizonte for five years, the statement added.

With the expansion of the power transmission and distribution sector, sales are expected to reach $500 million next year or 50 percent of total local ABB sales projected for 1997 and a record for its Brazil unit, it said.
Last year, the sector accounted for $364 million of ABB Brazil's total sales of $853 million, a hike of 30 percent from 1995, it added. Investments in 1996 totalled $20 million.

"As we await the (power) sector's privatization, we are counting on the investments announced by the government, such as the North/South transmission line, construction of the third circuit at Itaipu (dam) and interconnections with Argentina and Venezuela," Terni was quoted as saying.
ABB has factories in Cravihnos, Guarulhos and Osasco in Sao Paulostate, Contagem in Minas Gerais and Cachoeirinha in Rio Grande do Sul.
